title: Cache With Time Limit
statement:
Write a class `TimeLimitedCache` that stores integer values under integer keys, where every entry lives only for a limited time. It has three methods:

- `set(key, value, duration)` stores `value` under `key` for the next `duration` milliseconds; after that the entry has expired and cannot be read any more. If `key` already holds an entry that has not expired, the new value and the new duration both replace the old ones. Return `true` when such an unexpired entry existed, and `false` otherwise.
- `get(key)` returns the value under `key` if that entry has not expired, and `-1` otherwise.
- `count()` returns how many unexpired entries the cache holds.

Each case gives three lists of the same length, `actions`, `values` and `timeDelays`: action `i` runs at `timeDelays[i]` ms with the arguments `values[i]`, and actions due at the same time run in index order. The first action is always `"TimeLimitedCache"` at 0 ms, which creates the cache; every other action is `"set"`, `"get"` or `"count"`. The answer lists the results in index order, with `null` for the constructor. Cases never run an action at the very millisecond an entry expires, so you never have to decide whether the expiry or the action comes first.
constraints: No action runs at the exact millisecond an entry expires
signature: List<Object> TimeLimitedCache(String[] actions, List<List<Integer>> values, int[] timeDelays)
api: class TimeLimitedCache { set(key: number, value: number, duration: number): boolean; get(key: number): number; count(): number }
notes:
## Intuition

Every entry has to disappear when its time is up. There are two classic ways to get that. One lets a timer remove the entry the moment it expires, so the cache only ever holds live entries. The other stores each entry's expiry time and treats anything past it as missing whenever it is read. The reference uses timers, which fits JavaScript's `setTimeout` well: a `Map` holds each key's `value` together with the id of the `timer` that will delete it. When a key is written again, its old timer must be cancelled, or it would delete the new value too early. (The brute force takes the second way: it keeps expiry times and compares them with `Date.now()` on every call.)

## Approach

1. `cache` maps each key to `{ value, timer }`; only unexpired entries are in it.
2. `set` looks up `existing`. If there is one, `clearTimeout(existing.timer)` cancels its pending deletion.
3. It schedules a new `timer` that deletes the key after `duration` ms, and stores `{ value, timer }`.
4. It returns whether `existing` was found, which means an unexpired entry was replaced.
5. `get` returns the stored `value`, or `-1` when the key is absent.
6. `count` returns `cache.size`, since expired entries have already been deleted.

## Example 1, step by step

- 0 ms: the cache is created. `set(1, 42, 100)` finds nothing under key 1, returns `false`, and schedules key 1's deletion for 100 ms.
- 50 ms: `get(1)` returns `42`, and `count()` returns `1`.
- 100 ms: the timer fires and deletes key 1.
- 150 ms: `get(1)` finds nothing and returns `-1`. The answer is `[null, false, 42, 1, -1]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(1) per call: a few `Map` operations and at most one timer scheduled and one cancelled.
- Space: O(k) for the k unexpired entries and their pending timers.

## Pitfalls

- Overwriting a key without `clearTimeout`: the old timer still fires and deletes the new value. In Example 2 the timer from `set(1, 42, 50)` would erase the value `50` at 50 ms.
- With stored expiry times instead of timers, `count` must skip expired entries; the number of stored keys includes dead ones.
- `set` must return `true` only for an entry that is still alive. With stored expiry times, a key that is present but expired counts as absent.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `cache` | map from key to `{ value, timer }` for every unexpired entry |
| `existing` | the entry `set` replaces, or `undefined` |
| `timer` | id of the timeout that deletes the key when its duration ends |
| `entry` | the entry `get` finds, or `undefined` |

narration.3: cache only ever holds unexpired entries: each one is deleted by its own timer.
narration.7: Is there an entry for this key that has not expired yet?
narration.9: Cancel its pending deletion, or that timer would later erase the new value.
narration.11: Schedule this entry's deletion for duration ms from now.
narration.12: Store the value with its timer id, replacing any older entry.
narration.13: true exactly when an unexpired entry was replaced.
narration.18: An absent key has expired or was never set, so the answer is -1.
narration.22: Expired entries were deleted by their timers, so the size is the number of live entries.
